course.title: FatTail Labs: The Operating System
course.subtitle: Journey, Practice, Wiki, Strategy Lab, and Toughness — life routines, trained will, honest process
course.description_md:
FatTail Labs is not a content dump. It is an **operating system for trader development**: tools and programs that turn daily work into durable habits and skills.

This course is the map. Each lesson starts with a short **intro video**, then **step-by-step directions** for the feature or surface you just saw.

**The through-line is Journey.** Journey is not “another Practice app.” Every part of Labs you actually use — courses, live sessions, Practice (Trade Log, Journal, Retrospective, Reports), Wiki study, Strategy Lab work, and Toughness — shapes **Process Flow** — the flow state of your trading process. Practice is where the day-to-day trading loop lives; Journey is where that state stays honest and current.

**Toughness is bigger than the sprints.** The Hard 20 / 40 / 75 programs are **training exercises** — deliberate challenge to develop mental toughness, associated with the **anterior mid-cingulate cortex (aMCC)**. The real program is the **life routines and habits** you construct around that training so follow-through becomes natural. **Trading routines are not separate from life** — they are routines you enable the same way you enable sleep, training, and review.

**What you will be able to do**

- Explain what Labs is for (capacity over dependency; process over P&L theater)
- Use Journey as your path + process integrity surface
- Run the Practice suite with shared context (account + date)
- Treat Toughness as life-system design, with sprints as brain training — not as a streak contest
- Navigate Wiki and Strategy Lab without getting lost
- See how each surface feeds your Journey score

content_blocks.body_md:
## Outline (author me)

### What Process Flow is
- A **state of being** — the **flow state of your trading process**
- **Not** “the score you got after a test”
- Private standing of whether process is coherent and **current**
- New members: **Establishing** — empty ≠ failure; no day-one identity attack

### Why the name matters
Integrity as a quiz number invites gaming and shame. **Flow** invites: am I in process right now, and is recent life holding the stack?

### How it is measured (member-safe explanation)
1. **Pillars** (dimensions) — each reflects a part of process life:
   - Learning rhythm
   - Live presence
   - Practice persistence (Trade Log / Journal / tools)
   - Daily routine
   - Process adherence (plan-following on tagged trades)
   - Retrospective cadence
   - Mental toughness / Toughness when you engage it
2. **Weights** — key quality pillars (adherence, retrospective, …) count for more than pure show-up
3. **Exponential / recent emphasis** — more recent weeks weigh more than old history (EWMA-style). Drift shows up; ancient good weeks do not forever prop a broken present
4. **Grades / labels** describe the **state of flow**, not an exam grade for your worth

### What does *not* move Process Flow
- P&L, win rate, profit claims, peer rank

### Honest use
- Notice drift early → reinstall routine (life + trading same capacity)
- One process action beats chasing a prettier number

### Do this now
- [ ] Open Journey → Process Flow (or Process Integrity if UI not renamed yet)
- [ ] Name your weakest pillar this week
- [ ] One concrete Practice or life-stack action (not bigger size)

---
*Author: process outcomes only. Product: DL-190 + Process Flow repositioning note. As-built may still label Process Integrity until cutover.*

## Outline (author me)

### Open Retrospective
- **Practice → Retrospective** (`/app/retrospective`)

### What it is
- Structured review: what held, what broke, what you commit next
- Process first; results secondary — never the headline as a brag

### Surfaces
- **Library** of past retrospectives
- **Scope** — from last review (or maiden journey)
- **Ceremony** — dual report / steps through cause, what worked, next commitments
- **Cadence** — gentle nudges when a review is due (including from Journey)

### How to run one (step-by-step)
1. Confirm scope dates and what material is included
2. Walk the ceremony steps without skipping the “what broke” section
3. Write commitments you can keep next week (small, process-shaped)
4. Save and return to the library

### Link from Journal
- Material marked in Journal should appear in the ceremony inputs (confirm product wording)

### Do this now
- [ ] If you have ≥1 week of notes/trades: start a Retrospective
- [ ] If not: schedule the first retro date and keep journaling until then

---
*Weekly cadence is the default habit; adjust honestly to your calendar.*

## Outline (author me)

### Open Toughness
- **Apps → Toughness** (hub)

### The real program
Toughness is the **overall life routines and habits** you construct so follow-through becomes who you are — sleep, training, food, recovery, review, community, and the trading process you keep when nobody is watching.

That architecture is what supports **ultimate success**. The calendar sprints are not the destination.

### What the sprints are (preview — next lessons go deep)
- **Hard 20 / 40 / 75** = deliberate **training exercises**
- They train **mental toughness** under voluntary difficulty
- They sit *inside* the life-routine system; they do not replace it

### What Toughness is not
- Not “I finished 75 so I’m done”
- Not a profit program or signal service
- Not a substitute for medical care, therapy, or rest when those are what you need
- Not a shame machine for missing a day

### Product lexicon
- Member UI: **mental toughness** / **Hard** — not “tenacity” branding

### Do this now
- [ ] Open the Toughness hub and skim the whole surface, not only enroll buttons
- [ ] List 3–5 **life** routines you already depend on (or need)
- [ ] Mark which ones are solid vs aspirational — before you touch a sprint

content_blocks.body_md:
## Outline (author me)

### Why the sprints exist (Coach thesis)
Hard and related deliberate-challenge protocols train **persistence and willpower** — **mental toughness** — by repeating voluntary difficulty.

Literature associates that capacity with the **anterior mid-cingulate cortex (aMCC)** (sometimes popularized as a “willpower muscle”). Product maps the paper’s “tenacity” language to **mental toughness** in member UI.

### What you tell members (allowed shape)
1. **What** is trained: mental toughness — persisting when effort is costly
2. **Where** literature situates it: **aMCC**
3. **How** Labs applies it: repeated voluntary challenge (Hard ladder)
4. **What is not claimed:** we do **not** guarantee your aMCC will grow, thicken, or “level up”
5. Cite / attribute (example framing): Touroutoglou et al., 2020, *Cortex* — paraphrase, don’t invent papers

### Honest science posture
- Education, not diagnosis
- 75 Hard / selection culture = **practice analogues**, not peer-reviewed proof that Labs rewired anyone’s cortex
- Physiology copy on the hub stays cite-backed (product requirement)

### The developmental claim that *is* on-thesis
As you train under load, the **routines you build around the sprints** — timing, recovery, logging, showing up again after friction — become more **natural**. That is the point: capacity in life, not a badge.

### Do this now
- [ ] Read the hub’s physiology / how-it-works cite block once, slowly
- [ ] Write one sentence: “I am training mental toughness so that ____ becomes easier without willpower theater.”

---
*Ship gates: Hotel/Tango on any expanded aMCC curriculum; never profit claims; never medical guarantees.*

content_blocks.body_md:
## Outline (author me)

### Stimulus vs system
| Piece | Role |
|-------|------|
| **Sprint days** | Training load — deliberate difficulty |
| **Routines around the sprint** | Sleep window, movement, meals, shutdown, review, who you tell |
| **What “sticks”** | The stack becomes default as capacity grows — not the selfie of day 75 |

### Design the stack first
Before enrolling, answer:
1. When do I sleep and wake on a hard day?
2. What movement / challenge rules am I actually running?
3. When do I review (Journal / retro) relative to market hours?
4. What happens when life hits (travel, illness, family)?

### Naturalization
- Early days: high friction, high intention
- Later: the same actions cost less internal argument — that is the training working in life, not magic
- If the stack is fantasy, the sprint only produces burnout

### Do this now
- [ ] Write a one-page **life stack** for a Hard day (morning → market → evening)
- [ ] Circle the one item most likely to break; redesign it before you enroll

---
*Connect to Practice: Journal can hold the stack notes; Retrospective reviews whether the stack held.*

## Outline (author me)

### One life, one capacity
Trading routines are **not separate from your life**. They are routines you **enable** the same way you enable training days, sleep, and recovery.

| Life routine | Trading twin in Labs |
|--------------|----------------------|
| Show up when it’s hard | Log the trade you don’t want to look at |
| Honest review | Journal + Retrospective |
| Track the path | Reports + Journey Process Flow |
| Protect the body/mind | Position size, stop the bleeding, no revenge spiral |

### What this ends
- “I’m disciplined at the gym but chaotic in the book” as two identities
- Treating Practice apps as homework for a persona that only exists 9:30–4:00

### What this starts
- Same mental toughness for boring process as for hard workouts
- Journey as a read on **whole-life process**, not a trader cosplay scoreboard

### Do this now
- [ ] Name one non-trading routine that already works for you
- [ ] Attach one trading twin to it (same time block, same “non-negotiable” rule)
- [ ] Put the pair in Journal for this week

## Outline (author me)

### Placement
You only enroll **after** you understand Toughness as life routines + aMCC-framed training. Sprints are the **gym set**, not the life.

### The ladder (training load)
| Program | Shape | Training intent |
|---------|--------|-----------------|
| **Hard 20** | Entry load | Prove you can start and finish a short block |
| **Hard 40** | Stretch load | Consistency under more days |
| **Hard 75** | Peak optional | Only after lower rungs hold in *life*, not just calendar |

### How it works (member directions)
1. Watch how-it-works on the hub
2. Confirm your **life stack** (lesson 6.3) is realistic
3. Choose the lowest rung that still challenges you
4. Track daily honestly
5. **Miss → day one** (product rule — explain without shame theater)
6. Life events: pauses / restarts per shipped product behavior

### Ladder psychology
- Completing 20 with a real stack beats failing 75 for applause
- The win is **capacity and natural routines**, not the number on the badge

### Do this now
- [ ] If not ready: stay in life-stack design + Practice loop; no forced enroll
- [ ] If ready: enroll in the lowest honest rung; schedule the first week’s stack on the calendar
